cities.base: The historic district between Bright Angel Lodge and El Tovar. It is the only place on this trip where you can walk out of your room and be on the rim in ninety seconds, which is the whole argument fo
cities.name: Grand Canyon Village (South Rim)

cities.base: The single strip of Highway 64 south of the park entrance. Two blocks long, all hotels and franchise food, 7 miles and about fifteen minutes from Mather Point. You stay here when the in-park lodges ar
cities.name: Tusayan

cities.base: No beds worth planning around, only a seasonal first-come campground, a market and a gas station. You come for the 23 miles of Desert View Drive east from the Village: Grandview, Moran, Lipan, Navajo
cities.name: Desert View and the East Rim Drive

cities.base: Day use only in 2026. The Dragon Bravo Fire destroyed Grand Canyon Lodge in July 2025 and there is no overnight lodging on the North Rim this season; the campground reopened June 1 and the General Sto
cities.name: North Rim

cities.base: Downtown around Heritage Square and San Francisco Street. Everything you would actually want to eat or drink on this trip is inside six walkable blocks, and it is 80 miles to the rim, so use it at the
cities.name: Flagstaff

cities.base: The four blocks of old Route 66 between the Santa Fe depot and Grand Canyon Boulevard. Cheapest beds within an hour of the rim, and the only place you can board a train that puts you at the canyon wit
cities.name: Williams

places.name: Mather Point
places.note: The first canyon most people ever see and the single most crowded railing in the park; go at first light or walk ten minutes west along the Rim Trail and it empties out. NPS lists the South Rim open 24 hours, all year; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Grand Canyon Visitor Center
places.note: Open 09:00 to 16:00 daily this winter, no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price. Worth twenty minutes for the day's trail closure board and the shuttle map, both of which change week to week.

places.name: Yavapai Geology Museum
places.note: Built in 1928, a glass wall aimed down the canyon with the rock layers named in front of you, plus a relief map; the Trail of Time starts 650 feet west. Open 08:00 to 18:00, no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Rim Trail, Mather Point to Yavapai Point
places.note: Paved, flat, 1.4 miles, and the shuttle will bring you back, so it is the one rim walk that works for anyone regardless of fitness. NPS lists the South Rim open 24 hours, all year.

places.name: Bright Angel Trail to Three-Mile Resthouse
places.note: Six miles round trip with 2,100 feet of climbing on the way back; the trail is currently closed below the Tonto junction and most inner-canyon water taps are off, so carry all of it. NPS lists the South Rim open 24 hours, all year.

places.name: South Kaibab Trail to Ooh Aah Point
places.note: 1.8 miles round trip to the best cheap view in the park; no private cars at the trailhead, so take the orange shuttle or the Hikers Express from Bright Angel Lodge. NPS lists the South Rim open 24 hours, all year.

places.name: Shoshone Point
places.note: An unsigned 2.2-mile round trip on a flat dirt road to a rim promontory with a picnic table and usually nobody; park at the small unmarked pullout and do not block the gate.

places.name: Hopi Point
places.note: The classic sunset stop, which means the last red shuttle back is a scrum; Mohave Point one stop along gets nearly the same light with half the people. NPS lists the South Rim open 24 hours, all year; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Hermits Rest
places.note: Mary Colter's 1914 rest stop for Fred Harvey carriage tours, with a cave-like fireplace and a snack bar open 09:00 to 17:00. Cars may drive here December to February, otherwise the Red shuttle; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: El Tovar Dining Room
places.note: Closed for all meals per the park's 4 November 2026 update, with no reopening date posted. When it runs, the dark-timber 1905 room is the reason to come and the food is fine rather than good, so check the price.

places.name: Arizona Steakhouse
places.note: Dinner only for now, 17:00 to 20:30, with rim-facing windows; the boneless short ribs are $48 on the April 2026 menu and the skirt steak $40. Book on Tock up to 60 days ahead, since lunch is closed.

places.name: Harvey House Cafe at Bright Angel Lodge
places.note: Breakfast 08:30 to 11:00 and lunch to 15:30, dinner closed for now, no reservations. The double bacon cheeseburger is $20.50 and omelets about $15 on the July 2026 menus; the quickest meal before a trailhead.

places.name: El Tovar Lounge
places.note: Closed now per the park's 4 November 2026 update, no reopening date posted. When open, a small bar with a porch over the rim; get there before sunset for one of the four outside tables.

places.name: Fred Harvey Tavern
places.note: Closed now per the park's 4 November 2026 update, with no reopening date posted. When open, the Bright Angel Lodge bar where off-shift staff drink, with a $20.50 Tavern Burger on the July 2026 menu.

places.name: Hopi House
places.note: Colter's 1905 pueblo-form building, still a working gallery; the upstairs room holds serious Hopi and Navajo work at serious prices and most people never climb the stairs.

places.name: Kolb Studio
places.note: The Kolb brothers' 1905 studio, where their 1911 Colorado River film ran for decades. Exhibits are free, 08:00 to 18:00, the Celebration of Art runs to 31 March 2027, and free house tours need registering at 08:00 that day.

places.name: Lookout Studio
places.note: Mary Colter's 1914 stone lookout, built to compete with Kolb Studio, now a gift shop and terrace open 09:00 to 17:00; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price. The railing thirty feet away has the same view.

places.name: Verkamp's Visitor Center
places.note: A former family curio shop turned into a small exhibit on how people came to live on this rim; quiet, free, and five minutes from El Tovar.

places.name: Canyon Village Market
places.note: The park's only real grocery, plus a camping aisle with the electrolyte tabs and cheap headlamp you forgot; buy trail food here rather than in Tusayan.

places.name: Yavapai Lodge Tavern
places.note: Closed now, and no reopening date is posted as of November 2026. When it runs it is the least formal dinner in the park, with a big patio: the All-American burger is $17.99 and the elk chili $10.99.

places.name: Canyon Vista Mule Ride
places.note: Three hours along the rim, not down it, since the inner-canyon rides stopped with the flood; book months out and expect a weight limit and a saddle-sore afternoon.

places.name: IMAX Grand Canyon at the National Geographic Visitor Center
places.note: The 37-minute Rivers of Time film shows the river you will not otherwise see; $14 adult, $13 senior or military, $11 ages 6 to 10, plus tax. Winter shows run 10:30 to 18:30; 11 to 20 November the 18:30 is America the Beautiful.

places.name: Big E Steakhouse and Saloon
places.note: Mesquite grill, a proper bar and live music some nights; the best actual dinner in Tusayan and the only one locals turn up for.

places.name: Plaza Bonita
places.note: Standard northern Arizona Mexican, generous plates, margaritas that do real work at 6,600 feet; fine after a long descent and back.

places.name: We Cook Pizza and Pasta
places.note: Cafeteria-plain room, decent pizza, salad bar, and it will feed four people for what two spend inside the park.

places.name: Canyon Star Restaurant and Saloon
places.note: Hotel restaurant with a fake-log interior that runs live country and Native American dance sets most summer evenings; the show is the point, not the menu.

places.name: Wagon Wheel Saloon
places.note: Upstairs bar over the Canyon Star, open late by Tusayan standards, which means about 11pm.

places.name: Squire Pub and Social
places.note: Bowling lanes, pool tables and a bar in a hotel basement; genuinely the only thing to do in Tusayan after dark if it is raining.

places.name: Grand Canyon Airport helicopter flights
places.note: Papillon and Maverick both fly 25 to 45 minute loops over the Dragon Corridor; it is expensive, noisy and the one way to grasp the scale in a single glance.

places.name: Tusayan Greenway
places.note: A paved 6.5-mile path through ponderosa from the Tusayan strip to the Visitor Center; walk or rent a bike and skip the entrance-gate queue entirely.

places.name: Desert View Watchtower
places.note: Colter's 1932 tower with Fred Kabotie's Hopi murals; admission is free, 09:00 to 17:00, and the upper floors run on a free ticket for 25 people at a time, 20 minutes each, last access 16:00, stairs shut 16:30.

places.name: Desert View Point
places.note: The easternmost overlook on the South Rim and the only one where you see the Colorado turn west and the Painted Desert behind you. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Navajo Point
places.note: Highest point on the South Rim at 7,498 feet, with the Watchtower framed against the canyon a mile east; almost everyone drives straight past it. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Lipan Point
places.note: The widest stretch of visible river anywhere on the rim, including Hance Rapid; the best sunset on the South Rim and a fraction of the Hopi Point crowd. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Moran Point
places.note: Named for the painter whose canvases helped get this made a park; the red Hakatai shale below is the most saturated colour on the East Rim. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Grandview Point
places.note: The rim's original tourist hotel stood here before the railway moved everything west; the drop off the front is the steepest on the South Rim. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Grandview Trail to Coconino Saddle
places.note: A steep unmaintained miners' trail on cobbled log cribbing, 1.6 miles round trip and 700 feet down; no water, no rangers, and genuinely exposed in places. NPS lists Desert View Drive open all year, 24 hours, unless snow shuts it.

places.name: Tusayan Ruin and Museum
places.note: Closed now: the museum is shut until further notice and the pueblo trail ran 2 April to 31 October 2026, 08:00 to 16:00. A small Ancestral Puebloan village from around 1185 AD, 3 miles west of the Watchtower; no separate fee listed beyond the park entrance fee, so check the price.

places.name: Desert View Market and Deli
places.note: Closed for the winter per the park's Desert View page, and the Trading Post with it, so bring lunch: there is no other food for 23 miles in either direction. Only the pay-at-pump gas runs 24 hours.

places.name: Desert View Trading Post
places.note: Closed for the winter per the park's Desert View page. When open, mostly souvenir stock with a small case of genuine Navajo silver near the till.

places.name: Cape Royal
places.note: A paved 0.8-mile round trip to the southernmost point on the North Rim, looking down the canyon in both directions; open in 2026 and the single best thing still standing up here. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Angels Window Overlook
places.note: A natural arch in the limestone with a railed walkway over the top of it, halfway along the Cape Royal path; not for anyone with a fear of exposure. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Point Imperial
places.note: Highest overlook in the park at 8,803 feet, facing Mount Hayden and the Marble Platform; reopened for 2026 and reached by a three-mile spur off the Cape Royal Road. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.
places.neighborhood: North Rim, Cape Royal Road spur

places.name: Vista Encantada
places.note: Picnic tables on the rim above Nankoweap Creek; bring your own food and water because there is neither anywhere on the North Rim in 2026. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Roosevelt Point
places.note: A 0.2-mile loop to a bench looking east over the Little Colorado confluence country; five minutes of effort and usually empty. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Walhalla Overlook
places.note: Straight down onto the Unkar Delta, where Ancestral Puebloans farmed beside the river; you can pick out the house outlines with binoculars. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Walhalla Glades Pueblo
places.note: Stone footings of a summer farming settlement right beside the road, opposite the overlook; two minutes off the tarmac and almost nobody stops. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Cliff Spring Trail
places.note: 0.8 miles round trip down a forested ravine to a dripping overhang, past a small granary; open in 2026 and the easiest real walk left on this rim. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Cape Final Trail
places.note: 4.2 miles round trip on nearly flat ground through ponderosa to a rim point with no railing; confirmed open for 2026 and you may well have it to yourself. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: North Rim General Store
places.note: Dry goods and grab-and-go only, May 15 to October 15; with the lodge gone this is the entire food supply on the North Rim, and it does not sell drinking water reliably. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: North Rim Campground
places.note: Reopened June 1, 2026 with portable toilets and no showers, laundry, dump station or campfires under Stage 2 restrictions; reserve on recreation.gov and bring all your water. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Bright Angel Point Trail
places.note: The North Rim's signature half-mile walk, closed for all of 2026 along with Widforss, Transept and Uncle Jim after the Dragon Bravo Fire; do not build a day around it. NPS lists limited fall operations 16 October to 30 November 2026, but snow can shut the road from late October, so check.

places.name: Lowell Observatory
places.note: Where Pluto was found in 1930, and the telescope viewing after dark is the actual reason to go; shut Tuesdays, and viewing needs clear sky so check the forecast.

places.name: Museum of Northern Arizona
places.note: The best Hopi, Navajo and Zuni collection on the Colorado Plateau in a 1930s stone building; last admission is 16:00 and two hours is the right dose.

places.name: Walnut Canyon Island Trail
places.note: 240 steps down to 25 cliff dwellings built into a limestone undercut; the climb back at 6,700 feet catches people out, and the trail closes early for ice in winter.

places.name: Sunset Crater Volcano Lava Flow Trail
places.note: A one-mile loop across black cinder and lava from the 1085 AD eruption; the $25 vehicle pass also covers Wupatki, 20 miles up the same loop road.

places.name: Wupatki Pueblo
places.note: A hundred-room masonry pueblo with a ballcourt and a blowhole, standing in open red desert; covered by the Sunset Crater pass and worth the 20-mile drive between them.

places.name: Riordan Mansion State Historic Park
places.note: A 1904 log-and-shingle Arts and Crafts duplex built for two timber-baron brothers, seen only on the hourly guided tour; capacity is small so reserve.

places.name: Historic downtown Flagstaff and Heritage Square
places.note: Six square blocks of brick storefronts, bookshops and gear shops with freight trains going through the middle every twenty minutes; the whole trip's only real street life.

places.name: Macy's European Coffeehouse
places.note: Roasting their own since 1980, vegetarian menu, student crowd and communal tables; the most reliably good cup between Phoenix and the rim.

places.name: MartAnne's
places.note: Chilaquiles in a loud mural-covered room; the queue on a Saturday runs 45 minutes and it is the one Flagstaff breakfast worth waiting for.

places.name: Tinderbox Kitchen
places.note: The best cooking anywhere on this itinerary, and not by a small margin; book ahead, and the attached Annex bar will take you without one.

places.name: Pizzicletta
places.note: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza in a tiny room with a short natural wine list; there is a second counter inside Dark Sky Brewing if this one is full.

places.name: Mother Road Brewing
places.note: Flagstaff's anchor brewery, big patio, no kitchen so food trucks park outside; walkable from downtown and full of people who actually live here.

places.name: Arizona Snowbowl Scenic Gondola
places.note: Lifts you to 11,500 feet on Arizona's highest mountain with the canyon's north wall visible on a clear day; summer operation is Friday to Sunday only and pricing is demand-based.

places.name: Grand Canyon Railway Depot
places.note: 9:30am out, 5:45pm back, with a staged wild-west shootout before boarding that you can happily skip; coach fares run roughly $70 to $90 and premium cars well past $150.

places.name: Bearizona Wildlife Park
places.note: Drive your own car through wolf and bison enclosures then walk the bear area; $30 weekdays and $35 weekends, last car admitted at 16:00, and it earns its keep with kids.

places.name: Williams Historic Business District
places.note: Four blocks of neon, one-way Route 66 east and Railroad Avenue west; the last town on the old road to be bypassed by I-40, in 1984, and it has traded on it ever since.

places.name: The Sultana Bar
places.note: Oldest continuously licensed bar in Arizona, a former silent-movie house with a prohibition tunnel underneath; dark, cash-friendly and entirely unrenovated.

places.name: Red Raven Restaurant
places.note: The only place in Williams cooking with any ambition, a narrow room of about a dozen tables; reserve, because it fills the moment the train gets back.

places.name: Pine Country Restaurant
places.note: Diner food that is fine and about thirty pies made daily that are the actual point; order the pie first because the good ones go by mid-afternoon.

places.name: Cruiser's Route 66 Cafe
places.note: An old gas station turned barbecue hall with live music on the patio most summer nights; the theming is thick and the ribs are better than they need to be.

places.name: Grand Canyon Brewing and Distillery
places.note: The brewery whose beer you will see on tap at the canyon, with its own taproom and kitchen here; big, loud and reliably open when the strip has shut.

places.name: Williams Visitor Center at the Santa Fe Depot
places.note: A hundred-year-old depot with a small exhibit on the railway and the road; ten free minutes and the staff know which canyon roads are actually open today.

places.name: Canyon Coaster Adventure Park
places.note: An alpine coaster and a tubing hill on the edge of town; pure filler unless you have teenagers, in which case it buys you a peaceful evening.

places.name: Kaibab Lake
places.note: A small forest-service lake with a shoreline path and ponderosa on all sides; the one place near Williams that feels like northern Arizona rather than a film set.

places.name: Red Butte Trail
places.note: A short, steep 1.25 miles each way to a 7,324 foot knob with a fire lookout, the Havasupai Wii'i Gdwiisa; allow 2 to 4 hours. Park at the informal pull-offs, no fee found, and snow on the road was not checked.
places.neighborhood: Kaibab National Forest, about 17 km south of Tusayan

places.name: Foodie Club
places.note: Counter service for breakfast burritos, tortas and carne asada fries, with espresso and a small patio; entrees run about $10 to $30, so $20 is the midpoint. Listed 06:30 to 21:00, later on another site, so hours vary, check.

places.name: Tusayan-Montane Campground nature trail
places.note: A very short trail, about 0.05 mile, in the campground formerly called Ten-X, which charges $20 a site. The Forest Service and campflare give different seasons and points, so check before going.
places.neighborhood: Tusayan-Montane (formerly Ten-X) Campground, about 2 miles s

outings.why: The best ridge walk in the park, out on an open spine with drops on both sides and no shade at all. Down is easy and lies to you; the 2,040 feet back up in afternoon sun is the real hike. There is no water on the trail, only at the trailhea
outings.name: South Kaibab to Skeleton Point
outings.season: Year round, but avoid 10am to 4pm from May to September
outings.fallback: Turn at Cedar Ridge, 3 miles round trip, and still get the ridge and the views.

outings.why: Nine miles round trip and 3,040 feet of climbing back out, through tunnels and switchbacks into cottonwood shade. As of September 2026 the trail is closed below the Tonto junction, so Havasupai Gardens is the end of the line. Check water st
outings.name: Bright Angel down to Havasupai Gardens
outings.season: Year round; crampons often needed on the top mile December t
outings.fallback: Three-Mile Resthouse and back, about 5 hours, same trail and most of the drama.

outings.why: Twelve miles and 950 metres of ascent to a flat tongue of Tapeats sandstone 1,300 feet above the Colorado. It is the longest legal day hike currently open and the park openly discourages it in summer heat. Start before 5am or do not start.
outings.name: Plateau Point out and back
outings.season: October to April for anyone sane
outings.fallback: Stop at Havasupai Gardens and skip the exposed 1.5-mile spur.

outings.why: Seven miles of west rim closed to private cars from March to November, so you ride the free red bus and hop off at nine overlooks. Walk the paved Rim Trail between Powell and Hopi, then bus the rest. The buses fill at sunset and you will qu
outings.name: the Hermit Road shuttle
outings.season: Shuttle runs roughly March 1 to November 30; you can drive i
outings.fallback: Ride straight to Hermits Rest, walk back to Pima Point, bus home.

outings.why: Twenty-three miles east with five overlooks, a 900-year-old pueblo and Mary Colter's tower at the end. You need your own car; no shuttle goes east of Yaki Point. The tower stairs run on a free first-come ticket with a 25-person cap.
outings.name: Desert View Drive to the Watchtower
outings.season: Year round; the road stays open in winter
outings.fallback: Grandview and Lipan only, about 3 hours, and you have seen the best two.

outings.why: The cheapest good hour in the park. Paved, flat, about 1.4 miles of rim between the two points, then the Yavapai Geology Museum's window wall when your hands get cold. Mather itself will have 200 people on it; walk five minutes west and it
outings.name: sunrise at Mather Point and the Rim Trail to Yavapai
outings.fallback: Skip Mather entirely and start at Yavapai Point, which faces the same light with a third of the crowd.

outings.why: Departs Williams 9:30am, at the rim 11:45am, leaves the canyon 3:30pm, back 5:45pm. Three and a quarter hours at the rim is enough for the Village and the Rim Trail and nothing else. It is a good day if you hate driving and a waste of one i
outings.name: the Grand Canyon Railway day trip from Williams
outings.season: Daily year round, with an earlier 8:30am departure in Novemb
outings.fallback: Drive the same 60 miles in an hour and get five more hours at the rim.

outings.why: The 23-mile Cape Royal Road and its overlooks are the North Rim you can still have in 2026. Bright Angel Point, Widforss, Transept and Uncle Jim are all closed from fire damage, there is no lodge, no restaurant and no drinking water. Carry
outings.name: Cape Royal and Point Imperial
outings.season: May 15 to roughly mid-October, weather permitting; the road
outings.fallback: Cape Royal and the Cliff Spring Trail only, about 4 hours, and skip the Point Imperial spur.

outings.why: A 35-mile loop off Highway 89 from a 1085 AD cinder cone down into red desert and the Wupatki pueblos. One $25 vehicle pass covers both monuments. Good half day for an arrival or departure day when you are already driving.
outings.name: the Sunset Crater and Wupatki loop
outings.season: Year round; the loop road can close briefly for snow
outings.fallback: Lava Flow Trail at Sunset Crater alone, about 2 hours from downtown.

outings.why: 240 steps down into a limestone gorge and a loop past cliff dwellings built into the undercuts. Under a mile but the climb back out at 6,700 feet is honest work. Ten miles from downtown Flagstaff.
outings.name: the Walnut Canyon Island Trail
outings.season: Year round; Island Trail can close for ice in winter
outings.fallback: The Rim Trail above it is flat, paved and still shows you two dwellings.

destination.name: Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona
destination.pitch: Seven days is enough to stop treating it as one overlook and start walking into it, as long as you sleep close to the rim for the sunrises and accept that the 2025 fire and the 2026 flood have taken real pieces of the park off the table.
destination.caveat: As of November 2026, Stage 4 water restrictions make the park day use only, with no lodge or campground nights inside, so sleep in Tusayan for now. Non-US residents 16 and over pay an extra $100 each unless they hold an annual pass, and the North Kaibab Trail is shut since the 29 August flood. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: There is no city here. Flagstaff is a college town with good beer and a working downtown, and that is as urban as this trip gets.
because.food: Park food is a captive-audience operation, and Flagstaff an hour south is the only place on this trip where eating is a reason to be somewhere.
because.nature: A mile of exposed rock layers going back nearly two billion years, and the light on it changes every twenty minutes from first sun to last.
because.culture: Mary Colter's Watchtower, Hopi House and Lookout Studio, plus Tusayan Ruin and the Wupatki pueblos, are the built record of how people have read this landscape for 900 years.
because.adventure: South Kaibab to Skeleton Point and Bright Angel to Plateau Point are genuine mountain descents done backwards, with the hard half at the end.
because.relaxation: Sitting on a rim bench at Shoshone Point or Cape Royal with nobody in sight is the most restful thing here, but you have to drive away from the Village to get it.
because.exploration: Desert View Drive, Hermit Road and the two corridor trails give you four completely different angles on the same canyon within an hour of each other.
